title: introduce-invocation-context-hasher-and-drift-aware-alerts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Alert noise from token-cost and latency spikiness is often driven by repeated, near-duplicate prompt shapes and small config differences (quantization, seq_len, model variant). On incidents we repeatedly see many invocations that differ only in a few context tokens or client-side flags—this makes grouping noisy and rules brittle. This change introduces a lightweight invocation context hasher (config + prompt shape fingerprint) to group similar invocations, surface drift signals for prompt/token-shape distribution, and wire those signals into the alerting pipeline for adaptive alert suppression and automated reclassification of noisy bursts.

What this PR does (high level): add a deterministic invocation context hasher that emits a 64-bit stable fingerprint attached to traces and metrics; record per-fingerprint rollup metrics (invocation_count, p50/p95 latency, token_cost_mean, kv_cache_hit_rate); introduce drift detectors that compare recent fingerprint distributions against a rolling baseline and emit an anomaly tag; add a dashboard and exploration panels for fingerprint cohorts; add an alert tuning adapter that can downweight or suppress alerts when a single fingerprint accounts for >80% of cost/latency in the window (configurable).

Key goals: reduce alert churn from repetitive prompts, provide engineers a stable grouping key for triage, surface prompt-shape and model-config drift early, and keep overhead minimal (sampling and compact hashes).

Implementation notes: the hasher is a compact, collision-aware mix of: model identifier (model_id + quantization profile), sequence-length histogram (binned), top-k prompt token shape signature (shingled FNV64 over the first/last N tokens), and a small invocation feature vector (user_flags, streaming_mode, tool_calls_present). The hasher lives in the telemetry pipeline (in server-side pre-processor) and is attached as invocation.fingerprint to OTLP spans and metrics. Rollups are implemented as a new aggregation path that keeps reservoir sketches keyed by fingerprint for a 1h/24h window. Drift detector uses a lightweight JS divergence approximation and emits fingerprint.drift_score > 0.0 as a boolean tag after thresholding.

Backwards compatibility & privacy: fingerprint is not reversible; prompt tokens are not stored or transmitted. The fingerprint is a 64-bit hex string and should be treated as an opaque grouping key. We document PII considerations in the privacy section of the runbook.

Checklist:
- [x] runtime: context hasher implementation (Rust) with feature flag
- [x] telemetry: OTLP span/metric enrichment and schema bump
- [x] aggregation: add fingerprint-keyed rollups and reservoir sketches
- [x] dashboard: new fingerprint cohort panel + drift timeline
- [x] alerts: adapter to suppress alarms for single-fingerprint storms
- [x] tests: unit, integration, and end-to-end replay tests
- [x] docs/runbook: triage guidance and privacy notes

How to validate locally: follow observability/README.md run-local pipeline, set FEATURE_CONTEXT_HASHER=1, run replaybench against samples/observability/large-burst-cases.json, then open the dashboard at http://localhost:9090/d/fingerprint-cohorts.

Related work: builds on ENG-1953 (invocation cohorting prototype) and complements the alert-hysteresis work (ENG-2314). Incident INT-707 motivated the >80% cohort suppression heuristic.

Risks and mitigations: risk — collisions cause distinct prompts to join the same cohort. Mitigation — we added a collision monitor that emits fingerprint_collision_count and a sampling debug span with unhashed short token prefixes for the small percentage of flagged samples (opt-in). Performance risk — extra aggregation; mitigation — we used compact 64-bit keys and reservoir sketches to keep memory bounded.

Release notes: Adds invocation.fingerprint for telemetry, a fingerprint cohort dashboard, and a configurable alert adapter to suppress single-fingerprint storm noise.
